post.summary: Draft criteria from a job description
post.description:
Revcenter's reading of a job description as criteria, the way the app drafts a search: review it, change what the person asks, then launch it as criteria. Launches nothing. The same reading the app's composer makes: titles and their closest synonyms, the role's own place and radius, years, and requirements as short terms, with the rest as scored context. `review.warnings` names anything to check before launching (a place wider than the role's own); `compiled_query` is the exact query the criteria will send. Pass `project_id` to check the place against the project's name too. A PDF, Word (.docx) or text file can be sent instead of text as `document_base64` with its `document_type`: its text is read where it arrives and stored nowhere, and `document` says how much was read. Does not use credits. Let it run up to 60 seconds. Safe to retry: repeating it changes nothing more.

Needs scope `searches:write`.

post.description:
Start a LinkedIn search in a project, on `criteria` as sent (a `brief` in the person's own words fills what they leave unsaid), or on a `jd_text` Revcenter reads; with database_only it buys no new results pages (3 credits per profile delivered; people the workspace already has are free). Send an Idempotency-Key: a retry with the same key, project and body returns the same search; the same key on a different request returns 409 idempotency_key_reused. max_credits (250 to 20,000; absent, the workspace's limit per search; held to that limit (1,000 on a trial; on a plan 5,000 unless the workspace's admins set another) and to the credits left, with credits_note saying so; below 250 is refused with 400 max_credits_too_low) is reserved at launch and refused with 402 shortlist_allocation_exhausted when the workspace can't cover it (402 trial_used_up once a free trial is used up); when the search finishes it is charged 3 credits for each profile it delivered (people the workspace already has are free; results pages, lookups and AI screening cost nothing), never more than max_credits, and the rest comes back (get_search credits_charged and credits_breakdown). A search that fails is refunded in full. Reserves up to max_credits credits (by default the workspace's limit per search, in get_usage); unused credits are refunded. Let it run up to 60 seconds. Safe to retry with the same Idempotency-Key, which returns the first result; without one a retry can run it twice.

Needs scope `searches:write`.

jd_text.description: A job description, when not sending criteria.

brief.description: The person's own words about the role, as they wrote them, sent with criteria. Revcenter applies the app's rules to them where the criteria are silent: "no visa sponsorship" sets signal_options.needs_sponsorship, a typed title rule (AND/OR/NOT) sets title_boolean, a "Keywords:" rule sets keyword_boolean, and "ex-", "only at" or "not from" before a preferred employer sets employers. Fields the criteria set are never changed.

database_only.description: Buy no new results pages. Reserves max_credits like any search; 3 credits for each profile delivered, and people the workspace already has are free.

max_credits.description: The most this search may use, in credits: reserved now, charged 3 credits for each profile it delivers (people the workspace already has are free), and the rest refunded when it finishes. Leave it out to use the workspace's limit per search. Held to that limit (1,000 on a trial; on a plan 5,000 unless the workspace's admins set another; get_usage shows the workspace's own) and to the credits left; credits_reserved and credits_note say when it was held. At least 250. Send the amount the person names; any whole number in range works.

get.summary: Download every record a search returned as CSV
get.description:
Every record a search returned as CSV, one row per person in the order returned: status, score, page, name, title, company, location, LinkedIn address, summary and headline, and the read profile's experience, education and skills as text columns and as numbered columns; or as JSON Lines with format=jsonl. Columns after do_not_contact: headline, signals, about, experience_history, education, skills, certifications, languages, projects, connections, then the career as numbered columns (total_experience_months, current_role_months, experience_1_title, experience_1_company, experience_1_location, experience_1_start, experience_1_end, experience_1_months, experience_1_description … education_1_school, education_1_degree, education_1_field, education_1_start, education_1_end …), as many as the most roles and schools anyone in the file has: nothing is cut off, then first_seen_at, last_seen_at, profile_as_of, rationale, score_breakdown, the six criteria (criteria_title … criteria_move_readiness), verdict and the latest decision (decision, decision_reasons, decision_notes, decision_by, decided_at), listing_json (the search result row) and profile_json. UTF-8 with a byte order mark, so Excel reads it as written. columns picks the CSV's columns, in order (get_export_columns lists every key). ?format=jsonl returns JSON Lines instead: one person per line, lossless: the whole read profile (every role, school and section), the search result row for anyone never read, and Revcenter's person, current_role, career, education, scoring (score, every reading, rationale, signals, the six Verified/Missing criteria) and decisions keys; fields picks groups. For an AI agent, JSONL; CSV is for spreadsheets. No contact details on any export. Does not use credits. Let it run up to 120 seconds. Safe to retry: repeating it changes nothing more.

Needs scope `shortlists:read`.

Reserves max_credits like a launch. Without search_id: a new pass on the project's first search's criteria, once it has finished. Reserves up to max_credits credits (by default the workspace's limit per search, in get_usage); unused credits are refunded. Let it run up to 60 seconds. A camelCase key this answer shipped under before 2026-11-10 is still sent beside its snake_case name, holding the same value, and is deprecated.

shortlist_after_hash.description: Send it back as expected_shortlist_hash to apply exactly these people.

result.description: What preview_scoring or apply_scoring would have answered, once done.

ScoringDiagnostics.description: Keys are snake_case. A camelCase key this answer shipped under before 2026-11-10 is still sent beside its snake_case name, holding the same value, and is deprecated.

weights.description: The weights in force: the workspace's from Settings when an admin set them, else the search's own.

rejectReasons.description: Deprecated: the same as reject_reasons, with camelCase keys inside, kept for clients written before 2026-11-10.

penaltyReasons.description: Deprecated: the same as penalty_reasons, with camelCase keys inside, kept for clients written before 2026-11-10.

underFloorReasons.description: Deprecated: the same as under_floor_reasons, with camelCase keys inside, kept for clients written before 2026-11-10.

mustHaves.description: Deprecated: the same as must_haves, with camelCase keys inside, kept for clients written before 2026-11-10.

nearMisses.description: Deprecated: the same as near_misses, with camelCase keys inside, kept for clients written before 2026-11-10.

belowCutoff.description: Deprecated: the same as below_cutoff, with camelCase keys inside, kept for clients written before 2026-11-10.

outsideLocation.description: Deprecated: the same as outside_location, with camelCase keys inside, kept for clients written before 2026-11-10.

preferredEmployer.description: Deprecated: the same as preferred_employer, with camelCase keys inside, kept for clients written before 2026-11-10.

code.description: Stable: every code is on the Errors page.

details.description: Structured specifics, when there are any (for example retry_after_seconds).

error.message: No search with that id in this workspace.

do_not_contact.description: On the do-not-contact list in force for one of their projects: kept here, labelled.

dollars_per_credit.description: What one credit costs on this plan: its price divided by its credits. Null without a plan (a trial, or credits granted by hand).

acts_as.description: The person this key acts as, and their role in the workspace now: an admin's key sees every project, an editor's only the projects they made. Null for a key with no member behind it.

credit_terms.description: What a search may hold and is charged in this workspace: quote these, not fixed numbers.

max_credits_per_search.description: The most one search or expansion reserves, and what it reserves when it names no max_credits.

max_credits_per_project.description: The most a project's searches and expansions use together.

credits_per_profile.description: Charged for each profile delivered to the workspace. People it already has are free.

profile_read_credits.description: The same as credits_per_profile, kept for older clients.

dollars_per_credit.description: What one credit costs on the workspace's plan. Null without a plan: quote credits only.

actions.description: Every action that spends credits, at its price: quote these, not fixed numbers.

CreditAction.description: One thing that spends credits, in the words the app uses.

key.description: Stable id: profile, company_found, company_signals, company_decision_makers, company_list_minimum.

name.description: e.g. "Read and score a new LinkedIn profile".

unit.description: What one charge counts: profile, company or list.

credits.description: Credits per unit; null when charged as used.

pricing.description: per_unit: each unit costs credits. added_per_unit: on top of finding the same company. minimum: the least a company list that finds anything is charged.

dollars.description: credits × dollars_per_credit; null without a plan.

CreditActionLine.description: One action a search was charged for.

action.description: The action's key in credit_terms.actions; results_page_v1, profile_read_v1 and company_list_v1 name charges at earlier prices, other_data anything charged as used.

quantity.description: Units charged; null for the list minimum or data charged as used.

credits_reserved.description: What applying it reserves; unused credits are refunded when the search finishes.

shortlist_credits.description: Deprecated: credits_reserved in thousands, from when searches were priced in shortlists. Read credits_reserved.

effect.description: What the action would do: the before/after for a scoring change, capacity and credits for a search. Keys are snake_case. A camelCase key this answer shipped under before 2026-11-10 is still sent beside its snake_case name, holding the same value, and is deprecated.

FilterSources.description: Every filter the draft carries, how it counts and where it came from. A filter narrows the search (must_match) or leaves people out (left_out) only when the request's own words name it, apart from the role's titles and its place; anything Revcenter inferred only ranks (ranks_higher) and is from "suggested". Show the suggested ones to the person before launching.

field.description: The criteria field (titles and place stand for title_variants and metro or allowed_metros).

strength.description: must_match narrows the search; ranks_higher only ranks; left_out keeps people out.

from.description: request: the request's words name it; suggested: Revcenter added it.

words.description: The request's words it came from; null when suggested.

why.description: A short line to show the person.

CriteriaReview.description: What Revcenter changed in criteria before running them, and what to check: the rules the app's composer applies.

changes.description: Corrections made, e.g. a requirement sentence moved from must_have to must_have_context.

warnings.description: Not corrected; show them to the person before launching.

credits_reserved.description: Credits held for this search: its max_credits as held to the workspace's limit and balance (a database_only search reserves like any other), or 0 in a workspace whose credits aren't metered.

credits_note.description: Present when the cap asked for was held lower: to the workspace's limit per search, the project's credit limit, or the credits left.

CreditBreakdown.description: A search's charge line by line at the price it reserved under, held to its cap: 3 credits for each new profile delivered (profiles × credits_per_profile), results pages free (credits_per_page 0). Searches reserved before 2026-11-10 show their own price (pages, and profiles read). So far while it runs. Null for a refunded search, a database-only one, or one charged before round prices.

pages.description: Results pages searched, up to 25 people each.

profiles.description: Profiles delivered and charged in this search: new to the workspace, whether read now or already held. People the workspace already has are not counted. The same as the search's profiles_delivered.

reads.description: Deprecated: the same as profiles, kept for older integrations. Not only profiles read.

other_credits.description: Other metered work, charged as used.

line.description: The arithmetic in words, e.g. "81 profiles × 3 = 243 credits"; for a company search, per action, e.g. "40 companies found × 2 + 20 with hiring signals × 5 = 180 credits".

actions.description: The charge as named actions, before the cap: every credit counted, with the name the app shows.

CompanyCredits.description: A company search's credits per data action, from the same rows its charge settled from: 2 credits per company found (listed, at any score), 5 more per company with hiring signals, 3 more per company with decision makers (signals and decision makers only where some turned up), and a list that delivers anything is charged at least 100. Companies already in the workspace's results, companies cut before they were read and staffing agencies removed are free. A list from before per-action prices shows only its total (pricing per_company_list). Null for a search for people.

list_minimum.description: Credits the 100-credit list minimum added; 0 when the actions came to more.

line.description: The spend per action in words, e.g. "Finding 80 · Hiring signals 200 · Decision makers 120".

view.description: Present on view=status: the light read, without criteria, advice or the credit breakdown.

stop_reason.description: Why it stopped. A search runs until one of these: budget_exhausted (used its cap), discovery_exhausted (LinkedIn had no more), page_cap (the most pages LinkedIn serves for one query), cap_too_small (its cap was too small to deliver a page's people: nothing charged, every credit refunded), few_matches (several results pages in a row listed nobody who fits: widen the title or place), duplicate_pages (LinkedIn kept returning people already listed, so it stopped rather than pay for repeats; the people it read may all fit), cancelled, failed. Searches that ran before 2026-10-26 may also show target_reached or low_yield.

profiles_read.description: Profiles this search read, including people the workspace already had.

profiles_delivered.description: People this search delivered to the workspace for the first time: the count it is charged for (3 credits each). People the workspace already had are not counted. So far while it runs; null for a search that wasn't priced per profile (one from before 2026-11-10, or one that reserved no credits).

shortlisted.description: How many people were on the project's shortlist when this search closed: the whole project's list, including people earlier searches found. Null while it runs.

delivered.description: Deprecated: the same number as shortlisted, kept for older integrations. It is not the charged count; read profiles_delivered for that.

shortlist_count.description: How many people are on the project's shortlist now: the number the app shows on the project, the Projects list and the agent page, and get_project's shortlisted. Null for a search with no project. In both views.

status_note.description: One sentence on why the search is not moving (waiting its turn, waiting for a free slot, gone quiet, interrupted) or why it ended with a short list (pages of people who don't fit, its credits used, everyone its criteria reach), and what to do next. The same sentence the app shows. Null when there is nothing to explain. In both views.

stop_detail.description: Why the search was refused before buying anything, in a sentence: a required employer that matched no company, or a place that did not resolve. Null otherwise.

queue.description: While the search waits its turn (status queued): about how many seconds until it starts. Null otherwise.

eta_seconds.description: About how many seconds until it starts.

credits_state.description: Where its credits stand, as get_spend says for the same search: held (running, its cap reserved), charged (finished and charged), refunded (its whole reservation came back), none (nothing was reserved). In both views.

credits_reserved.description: Credits held at launch (max_credits), a database-only search's included.

credits_charged.description: What the search was charged once it closed, never more than credits_reserved; the rest was refunded. Null while it runs; 0 for a finished search that reserved nothing. get_spend says the same for each search.

steps.description: What the search did, step by step, oldest first: the titles and places it searched, how many people the first page matched and any filter it widened or narrowed because of it, each round of profiles read, people left out for living outside the area, why it stopped, and the finished list. Each step is a plain sentence written from the search's own numbers, with a detail line, its counts and when it happened. The same steps the app's AI chat shows as Reasoning. Full view only; empty for searches that ran before steps were recorded.

kind.description: What kind of step: searching (the titles and places sent), on_file (people already in the workspace who fit), matched (how many people the first page matched), widened or narrowed (a filter changed because of that count), read (a round of profiles read), outside_area (people left out for where they live), stopped (why it stopped), done (the finished list), failed.

text.description: The step in a plain sentence, e.g. "Widened the company size because few people matched".

detail.description: A second line with the step's numbers or reason; null when there is none.

tone.description: warn marks a step that changed course or left people out; done the finished list; failed a search that ended without one.

counts.description: The step's numbers by name (read, pages, people, removed, shortlisted, total_read, total_pages, titles, places, screened_out); only the ones the step has.

advice.description: What to check before the list goes to a client, once it finishes, each a sentence to read: few people read (under 75), a search you stopped early, a query that matched more people than one search can list, or a place wider than a city. Empty when there is nothing to check.

do_not_contact.description: On the do-not-contact list in force for this project: kept here, labelled, and off the shortlist and the client's link.

fit.description: How the person reads on each criterion (title, location, years, skills…).

signals.description: The signals the app's Signals column shows: open_to_work, open_to_relocate (the move in the label), move_ready, job_hopper, very_senior, out_of_area, needs_sponsorship.

on_shortlist.description: On the project's live shortlist now: false for anyone hidden from it.

profile.description: The full read profile: experience, education, skills, certifications, languages, projects. No contact details.

candidate_id.description: The person's id in this workspace (as list_people, add_shortlist_members); null when this workspace has not read them.

status.description: scored: read and scored in this search. known: already in this workspace from another search. not_read: listed, never read.

page.description: The result page that listed them first.

do_not_contact.description: On the do-not-contact list in force for this project: kept here, labelled.

open_profile.description: Can be messaged without a connection.

profile.description: The full read profile, as list_people gives it; null when not read. No contact details.

allOf.description: status rolls up across the project's searches (scored beats known beats not_read); score is the best any of them gave.

first_search_id.description: The search whose page listed them first.

search_ids.description: Every search in the project that returned them, earliest first.

Criteria.description: The search's criteria: title_variants (or an employer with flag must) and a metro, allowed_metros or remote_ok at least. draft_criteria writes them from a job description; get_criteria_reference explains every field. Keep must_have to short literal terms (at most 5, each at most 6 words); prose goes in must_have_context. A single string where a list is taken is read as a one-item list. A field that isn't listed here is refused with 400 invalid_criteria, naming it. Deprecated fields are accepted from older clients; current tools don't write them.

family.description: Scored after a profile is read: a role family label. Never sent as a title.

title_variants.description: Filter, sent before any profile is bought: current job titles, literal, OR'd. The first is the role; it and its closest synonyms are sent (5 at most). Optional when an employer is a current must.

seniority.description: Filter, sent before any profile is bought: the level, sent with one level either side.

allowed_seniority.description: Filter, sent before any profile is bought: levels to accept, instead of seniority's one either side.

must_have.description: Scored after a profile is read: short literal terms a profile must show, matched as text: at most 5 terms of at most 6 words each, like "CPA" or "PE license". Prose goes in must_have_context.

must_have_context.description: Scored after a profile is read: requirements as prose, at most 10 items: context for screening, never matched as text.

search_titles.description: Filter, sent before any profile is bought: the exact titles to send instead of title_variants (at most 10), when the person edited the list.

title_requires.description: Filter, sent before any profile is bought: a title rule as groups that must all appear in the current title, any phrase per group: [["data center"], ["manager", "director"]] reads "data center" AND (manager OR director).

title_boolean.description: Filter, sent before any profile is bought: the title rule as written, at most 400 characters: AND, OR, NOT in capitals, brackets, "quoted phrases".

keyword_boolean.description: Filter, sent before any profile is bought: a keyword rule over the whole profile, as written: AND, OR, NOT in capitals, brackets, "quoted phrases"; at most 245 characters and 12 phrases, no commas.

industries.description: Scored after a profile is read: background industries that rank; for a current-employer filter use current_industries.

source_company_keywords.description: Scored after a profile is read: kinds of company the likely candidates come from; ranks, never gates.

metro.description: Filter, sent before any profile is bought: the role's own place: 'City, ST', a state or a country.

allowed_metros.description: Filter, sent before any profile is bought: more places, OR'd with metro.

location_anchor_zips.description: Scored after a profile is read: 5-digit ZIP codes the radius is measured from, at most 25.

geo_radius_mi.description: Scored after a profile is read: commute radius around metro, in miles.

remote_ok.description: Scored after a profile is read: true when the role is remote: location then doesn't gate.

exclude_titles.description: Current titles to leave out, sent as a filter before any profile is bought. A title that often shares one title with the role (Partner beside Principal) is not filtered: those people rank lower instead.

exclude_industries.description: Filter, sent before any profile is bought: current employer industries to leave out (LinkedIn industry names).

exclude_companies.description: Filter, sent before any profile is bought: current employers to leave out.

avoid_titles.description: Scored after a profile is read: titles to rank down, never reject.

avoid_industries.description: Scored after a profile is read: industries to rank down, never reject.

avoid_companies.description: Scored after a profile is read: employers to rank down, never reject.

comp_band.description: Scored after a profile is read: [low, high] annual pay, in USD.

years_experience.description: Filter, sent before any profile is bought: {min, max, ideal, basis: total|relevant, enforcement: hard|preferred}. Hard bands are sent; preferred only ranks.

permitted_gaps.description: Scored after a profile is read: gaps a Tier 2 match may have.

min_avg_tenure_years.description: Scored after a profile is read: the shortest average tenure that scores well, in years.

skills.description: Scored after a profile is read: skills that rank.

skills_required.description: Scored after a profile is read: hard skills; 'A or B' matches either.

languages_required.description: Scored after a profile is read: spoken languages the role needs.

signal_options.description: Scored after a profile is read: optional signals; needs_sponsorship true when the role can't sponsor a visa.

target_company_profile.description: Scored after a profile is read: the kind of employer preferred: sector, employee_range [min, max], pe_backed_preferred.

rubric_weights.description: Deprecated: scoring weights are a workspace setting an admin changes in Settings. A launch still accepts it from older clients and from criteria copied off an existing search (the workspace's weights win when an admin has set them); a scoring change that sends it is refused (weights_in_settings).

shortlist_min_score.description: Scored after a profile is read: the shortlist cut-off (default 80); a scoring change takes 50 to 85.

preferred_employers.description: Scored after a profile is read: employers that rank up (current +8, past +5); never a gate.

employers.description: Filter, sent before any profile is bought: named employers: {name, temporal: current|past|either, flag: must|prefer|exclude}. must and exclude filter; prefer only ranks.

past_titles.description: Filter, sent before any profile is bought: titles held before the current one.

company_headcount.description: Filter, sent before any profile is bought: current employer size bands, A (self-employed) to I (10,001+).

recently_changed_jobs.description: Filter, sent before any profile is bought: only people who changed jobs in the last 90 days.

market_coverage.description: Reach the whole market: a query matching more than LinkedIn's 2,500 per query is split into slices (employer size, then title, then level) that each fit. Each slice's first results page is a paid page.

current_industries.description: Filter, sent before any profile is bought: industries the current employer must be in (LinkedIn names, search_industries).

functions.description: Filter, sent before any profile is bought: LinkedIn job functions to include.

exclude_functions.description: Filter, sent before any profile is bought: LinkedIn job functions to leave out.

years_at_current_company.description: Filter, sent before any profile is bought: {min, max} years at the current employer.

schools.description: Filter, sent before any profile is bought: schools attended, by name.

exclude_schools.description: Filter, sent before any profile is bought: schools to leave out.

profile_languages.description: Filter, sent before any profile is bought: the language the profile is written in, not a spoken language.

keywords.description: Scored after a profile is read: words anywhere on the profile, scored after reading; to filter by words before reading, use keyword_boolean.

exclude_locations.description: Filter, sent before any profile is bought: places candidates must not be in.

company_hq_locations.description: Filter, sent before any profile is bought: where a candidate's current employer is headquartered ("Michigan", "Denmark").

degree_country.description: Scored after a profile is read: where a degree is from, by the school's LinkedIn id, only when asked: countries (ISO codes), level, flag must or prefer. Unknown is not verified, never a match or a failure. See GET /reference/criteria.
